question: verify-standards reports INDETERMINATE (a failing required check) whenever a pull request carries any formal review whose own commit is not the current head -- including a rate-limited CodeRabbit COMMENTED review left at an earlier head, which permanently wedged PRs #1297 and #1302 since a PR with no review at all passes cleanly. Should the review-evidence check's evaluability logic change, and if so, how?
options: Carve stale reviews out of the evaluability set entirely; report them on a new ReviewEvidenceReport.staleReviews field instead of forcing the whole check to indeterminate. A stale check or thread finding is NOT carved out -- only a stale review-record finding.
Keep indeterminate, but only for a stale review whose state is APPROVED or CHANGES_REQUESTED; a stale COMMENTED review (CodeRabbit's actual shape) carries no verdict.
Keep as-is; treat CodeRabbit's quota as a throughput limit to buy more of, or drop verify-standards from the required-context ruleset until fixed.
recommendation: Option 1 -- it is the most direct reading of the gate's own stated intent (a stale record folded into neither pass nor fail is indeterminate for that record, not for a run that has other, current evidence able to decide it on its own); option 2 still reproduces the exact CodeRabbit-COMMENTED failure mode and adds a second piece of state-dependent logic; option 3 fixes nothing structural and treats a defect in the check's own logic as an external capacity problem.
decision: Implemented option 1 on claude/review-evidence-stale-policy, scoped to packages/inspector/src/review-evidence.ts and verify.ts (the vendor-neutral validator in packages/controller is untouched). A stale review-record finding is excluded from checkReviewEvidence's evaluability list and surfaced on ReviewEvidenceReport.staleReviews instead; a stale APPROVED review still never counts toward requireApproval (it was already excluded from hasApproval); a stale check or thread finding is unaffected and still reports indeterminate. Tests added in packages/inspector/src/review-evidence.test.ts; the integration test in scripts/collect-review-evidence.integration.test.mjs updated from asserting indeterminate to asserting satisfied for this exact scenario. packages/inspector bumped 0.2.8 -> 0.2.10.
notes: Backfilled from issue #1311's own body, which the recommendation/options/decision text above is drawn from almost verbatim, and its 'Changes applied per the Opus second opinion' follow-up comment. decidedBy is 'consensus' per the task's own instruction and the decision-tier rule's tier-1 path (a first reviewer plus a stronger-model second opinion, both recommending acceptance with no unresolved finding). The reviewing sessions' exact instanceId and effort were not captured at the time this decision was made (predates governance/review-tiers.json and docs/contracts/review-record.json); provider/model are reconstructed from the issue's own text ('the Opus second opinion') where stated, and left as unrecorded-predates-schema where not -- see docs/contracts/decision-record.json's note on backfilled reviews[] entries. Classified tier-1 (a change to a required check's own evaluability logic -- gate-relaxing in shape, though it removes a false positive rather than a real safeguard), which is why a sunset was considered and rejected: the change corrects a bug in the gate's own logic (a stale, non-decisive record wedging an otherwise-passing run) rather than loosening a real control, so it carries no sunset -- there is no safeguard being time-boxed away.
